title: Saudi-Led Coalition Strikes Houthi-Held Hodeidah After Tanker Attack
detail: The Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi military sites in Yemen's Hodeidah governorate and telecommunications-authority facilities in Kamaran, a day after Houthis claimed responsibility for attacks on two Saudi-flagged vessels in the Red Sea, including the tanker NCC Masa, which sustained minor hull damage but continued its voyage. Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki called the Houthi attacks 'cowardly and reckless' and pledged continued operational action; a coalition spokesman said Hodeidah port itself was not targeted and Yemeni ports remained open. The Houthi foreign ministry warned the strikes would 'prove costly' for Riyadh. The exchange followed the Houthis' July 20 blockade declaration and their claimed ending of the informal 2022 truce.

media.caption: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi military sites in Hodeidah after Red Sea tanker attacks

title: US Imposes 12.5% Forced-Labor Tariff on Saudi Arabia
detail: The Office of the US Trade Representative imposed new Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5% on imports from 60 economies, including Saudi Arabia, after determining the countries had 'failed to impose and effectively enforce a forced labor import prohibition.' The action, part of a broader wave of Trump administration tariffs covering economies representing 99% of US imports, added a new economic headwind for Saudi Arabia as it was already absorbing an oil-revenue shortfall from the Iran war and Red Sea shipping disruptions.

media.caption: Trump's forced-labor tariffs hit Saudi Arabia among 60 economies
